title: Manyhands JSON v1 conflict resolution mutation data
description: The data of a conflict resolve envelope: the synchronization whose conflict the request resolved, the resolution commit, how far the publication that continued it got, and the next step of a conflict. A request that resolved and checkpointed the conflict names its commit; one refused because the conflict is to be repaired outside Manyhands names none, and its conflict says so. It holds no source and names no path.

type.description: The one value that tells this data apart.

operation_id.description: The synchronization, whichever ID the request named: its own, or the operation of a comment it publishes.

commit_oid.description: The resolution commit, whose parents are the conflict's local and incoming parents, in that order. Null when the request made none.

publication.description: As the envelope's publication effect says: published, current when the remote held the commit already, pending while the publication is still to be made, or not_requested for a request that resolved nothing.

conflict.description: The next step of a conflict: one the publication met in a merge of its own, left in the target worktree, or the conflict this request could not resolve in Manyhands. Null otherwise. It names no path and holds no content.

operation_id.description: The synchronization the conflict is of: operation_id.

next_action.description: resolve when every conflicted path is canonical content of one item, which can be resolved in Manyhands; external_repair when any is not, so the merge is finished in Git outside Manyhands.
